## Duplicated Code Findings

Found **8 clone groups** with duplicated blocks across cart and order code:

**JavaScript Cart Service (`cart.js`)**
Four nearly identical `$http` patterns with renamed variables (lines 19-29, 80-90, 95-105, 110-120):
- `checkout()`, `removeFromCart()`, `setCart()`, `addToCart()` all follow: `var deferred = $q.defer(); $http({...}).then(resolve/reject); return deferred.promise;`

**Java Cart & Order Services**
1. **CatalogService.getCatalogItems() ↔ OrderService.getOrders()** (5 stmts each)  
   Both use identical CriteriaQuery boilerplate with renamed types: `CriteriaBuilder cb = em.getCriteriaBuilder(); CriteriaQuery<T> criteria = cb.createQuery(T.class); Root<T> member = criteria.from(T.class); criteria.select(member); return em.createQuery(criteria).getResultList();`

2. **CartEndpoint.add() & set()** (lines 59-62, 90-93)  
   Both execute: `ShoppingCart cart = shoppingCartService.getShoppingCart(cartId); ... shoppingCartService.priceShoppingCart(cart); cart.setShoppingCartItemList(dedupeCartItems(...));`

3. **CartEndpoint.add() & set()** (lines 66-70 / Transformers.toProduct)  
   Both create entity objects with property setters.

4. **ShoppingCart.removeShoppingCartItem() & PromoService.getPromotions()** — Cross-domain duplication suggesting shared utility logic.

**Recommendation:** Extract the common `$http` deferred pattern in cart.js and the CriteriaQuery boilerplate in Java services into reusable helpers to reduce maintenance debt.

events.text: Which clone group is the best candidate for extraction into a shared helper, and why?

events.html:
Fragment 2 (JPA CriteriaQuery) is the best extraction candidate:

Why:

  1. Systemic pattern — Not just 2 services affected; every future service querying the database will copy this same 5-statement boilerplate. CatalogService and OrderService are the first; next will be InventoryService, PromoService, etc. Extracting now prevents 10+ future duplicates.
  1. Standard, bulletproof logic — Pure JPA utility with no domain-specific variation. The pattern is identical regardless of entity type. Contrast with Fragment 5 (cart pricing), where pricing logic may differ per use case.
  1. Low extraction cost, high ROI — Single generic method solves it:
   <T> List<T> findAll(Class<T> entityClass) {
       CriteriaBuilder cb = em.getCriteriaBuilder();
       CriteriaQuery<T> criteria = cb.createQuery(entityClass);
       Root<T> root = criteria.from(entityClass);
       criteria.select(root);
       return em.createQuery(criteria).getResultList();
   }

Then both services reduce to: findAll(CatalogItemEntity.class) / findAll(Order.class)

  1. Cross-file, cross-team impact — Fragment 1 (JS) is confined to cart.js; Fragment 5 is single class. This affects multiple Java services across the codebase.
  1. Maintenance multiplier — Bug in criteria query (e.g., missing .where(), n+1 problem) gets fixed once instead of across all services.

Implementation Path:

  • Create BaseService or JpaQueryHelper with generic findAll<T>
  • CatalogService, OrderService inherit (1 line each instead of 5)
  • Future services use it automatically
  • Frees developers from remembering the pattern

Run: rgctl -r . callers "CatalogService.getCatalogItems" --depth 2 to confirm call sites before refactoring.
